area.title: Journey flow, step order and what applies when
area.scope: How the notification journey hangs together across pages: the version mount and session, the step order and next-page rules, the opening run, change and return contexts (from hub, from review, from template review), the shared journey buttons and their actions, the status strip and reference, the obligations and scope rules saying which questions apply to which consignment and what is optional versus a hard stop, the end-to-end journeys walked whole, the prototype's route and coverage tables, and the decisions ledger. Stops at any one page's own content. Includes the high-risk plants frontend's flow, opening run, entry guard, section captions, feature registry, obligation set index and set mount, and the rest of its decisions ledger (standing rulings, parked behaviours, non-functional rulings).

sources.role: the owner's decisions: outranks every other source. Search boxes use the real frontend's accessible component with MDM's entries. JavaScript behaviour follows the toolbox rule with graceful degradation; JavaScript-only prototype behaviour, pop-ups included, waits on design in its own theme. Commodity catalogue and search wait on MDM; transporter management waits on requirements; the INS dashboard's summary information waits on its requirements. The overview, review, declaration and confirmation are set-owned, and shared parts change add-only. Where plants has the same page or behaviour, the same increment changes it. Each notification list is reframed in its own frontend. The report groups work as ready or blocked. Claims marked as the orchestrator's apply Sam's principles and are not his rulings; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-templates covers templates and the dashboard narrowing.

claims.statement: Sam rules that the prototype's search and autocomplete controls are not accessible and not production grade, because they are AI-generated prototype code rather than GDS components.

claims.statement: Sam rules that for a search box the precedence is not 'prototype always wins': the component used may be the one already in the real frontends, where it has been deemed accessible.
claims.quote: only use a version of auto complete or search or whatever that has been deemed accessible and meets our requirements. If it has been, the sort of precedence needs to be a little bit different than prototype always wins. In terms of the component being used, it might be the one that's actually in the frontend or frontends.

claims.statement: Sam rules that the prototype's JavaScript behaviour is not GDS compliant and is not to be blindly replicated by adding lots of JavaScript to the frontend, for accessibility and maintainability reasons.
claims.quote: the prototype is doing stuff with JavaScript that is not GDS compliant. This isn't stuff that can just be blindly replicated by chucking a tonne of JavaScript in the frontend. ... 'Do things like add all this JavaScript stuff for accessibility concerns and maintainability concerns.'

claims.statement: Sam rules that GDS components are the toolbox, and where one is not available another tested, accessible government library (such as Ministry of Justice or Scottish Government) is used.
claims.quote: We really try to strictly head here to GDS components as a toolbox, and where that's not available, use other government libraries like a Ministry of Justice or a Scottish Government component that has been tested and meets accessibility requirements.

claims.statement: Sam rules there is a graceful degradation requirement: CSS and JavaScript may enhance behaviour, but every page must work without JavaScript, so the prototype's way of doing things may not be possible or wanted in the real service.
claims.quote: We've got a graceful degradation requirement on this, like any other GDS project, which means you can use things like CSS and JavaScript to enhance behaviour, but you need graceful degradation. It needs to be able to work without JavaScript, and that means that the way things are done in the prototype may not be possible or even desired in the real thing.

claims.statement: Sam rules that, as a pre-step for these increments, three questions are answered: is it possible with off-the-shelf GDS; if not, with other complementary off-the-shelf components; if not, why is the atypical thing strongly required. At that point it goes back to design to push back.
claims.quote: Almost as a pre-step for some of these increments, we need to get answers to that stuff: - Is it possible using off-the-shelf GDS? - If it isn't, is it using available, off-the-shelf, other complementary components? - If it isn't, why is this atypical thing strongly required? At that point, we go back to design and say, 'Come on, we don't need this.'

claims.statement: A behaviour the prototype gives with JavaScript is built only if it passes these tests in order: GOV.UK Frontend's components and patterns first; then another tested government library (Ministry of Justice, HMRC, Scottish Government); otherwise it goes back to design, which must say why it is strongly needed.
claims.quote: GOV.UK Frontend's components and patterns are used first. Where they have nothing, another tested government library is used, such as the Ministry of Justice's, HMRC's or the Scottish Government's. Where neither has anything, the behaviour goes back to design, which must say why it is strongly needed.
claims.note: Marked 'Sam (point 3)'. HMRC is named in claim 5 but not in Sam's quote, which names Ministry of Justice and Scottish Government only; the examples are illustrative ('like').

claims.statement: Increments are grouped into themes, and the themes are drawn from the evidence.
claims.quote: Themes: group the increments into themes based on the evidence.
claims.note: New.

claims.statement: Each theme's boundary is set by the code it touches.
claims.quote: Draw the boundaries by the code each one touches
claims.note: New.

claims.statement: Themes can be built in parallel on separate machines without pull requests that conflict with each other.
claims.quote: so themes can be built in parallel on separate machines without conflicting PRs.
claims.note: New.

claims.statement: The ruling's DR1 paragraph has an elision marked [...]: what the omitted words said about the DR1 parity backlog is not recorded.
The ruling does not say what makes a difference 'truly exceptional', so when a question for people is warranted is left open.

The ruling limits DR1 use to clashes between 'the real frontend' and the prototype; it does not say which frontend that is, or whether DR1 judgements apply to differences in the INS frontend, the backends or other repos.
The ruling does not say which override wins when a DR1 judgement and a real constraint the prototype cannot express point different ways on the same difference.
The ruling does not say what a real service does where a real constraint overrides the prototype: whether it keeps today's behaviour or matches the prototype as closely as the constraint allows.
The ruling does not say whether a feature or behaviour a real service has that Design Release 2.1 does not show at all counts as a difference to remove, or is left alone.
The ruling does not say what to do where the code two themes need to touch overlaps, so no boundary keeps their pull requests from conflicting.

The hub is somewhere the user chooses
to go — through the secondary "Save and return to overview" button on every
page, or by opening the notification from the dashboard — not somewhere the run
puts them between sections.

claims.statement: Once the task list has been shown, the opening run is over: saving a page then moves through its own section and returns to the task list at the section's end.
claims.quote:
rendering it completes the run
([`completeOpeningRun`](../../../flow/run-state.js), called from
[`features/hub/controller.js`](../journeys/linear/features/hub/controller.js)).
After that, saving a page follows `nextInSection` and returns to the hub at the
end of each section: the run is not re-entered for that notification.

claims.statement: A run that reaches the review step while the notification is incomplete, or whose remaining steps are all closed, falls through to the task list.
claims.quote:
The review
step
carries the same authored gate the review flow section does, so a run that
arrives with the notification incomplete falls through to the hub; so does a run
whose remaining steps are all gated out.

claims.statement: The opening run begins only when a notification is created from the dashboard; the origin page is the journey's entry page.
claims.quote:
The opening run begins when the notification is created — the dashboard's
create POST in
[`features/dashboard/controller.js`](../journeys/linear/features/dashboard/controller.js)
is the only caller of `beginOpeningRun`. The origin page is the journey entry

claims.statement: A deep link to a notification this session never created and that holds no answers is redirected to the origin page; the origin page itself is exempt.
claims.quote:
The guard admits a request when the opening run has begun for that journey in
this session, or the journey carries committed user answers. A journey with
neither — a deep link to an id this session never created and that holds no
answers — is sent to the origin page.

claims.statement: Existing ruling: a returning user without run state who saves the origin page goes to the task list rather than into the opening run; only a notification created in this session runs through the sequence.
claims.quote:
That is the accepted
rule for a returning user without run state: they land on the task list and work
from there. Only a notification created in this session sequences through
`RUN_STEPS`.

claims.statement: Each page shows a section caption directly above its heading, sized to match the heading, naming the part of the notification it belongs to.
claims.quote:
files every page under the section of the notification it belongs to, and names
those sections in its own `copy/` bundles.

claims.statement: Caption sections are finer than the task-list groups: animal identification is captioned with the other consignment questions, and arrival, transit and adding a transporter each have their own caption; a page left out of the caption map shows none.
claims.quote:
the caption keeps
animal identification with the other consignment questions and separates arrival,
transit and adding a transporter, where the hub does not. A page left out of the
map renders no caption;

claims.statement: Only the dashboard, declaration and confirmation pages sit outside the opening run; any other question page left out of the run is skipped while the run is active and reachable only from its task row.
claims.quote:
every new question page gets
a `RUN_STEPS` entry unless it is deliberately outside the run (the dashboard,
declaration and confirmation are the only ones today) — a page left out is jumped
straight over while the run is active and is reachable only from its hub row.

claims.statement: Existing ruling (design release 1): task rows carry no hint, except "Roles and addresses", which is the one hinted row.
claims.quote:
Hub task rows carry no hint:
Design release 1 keeps the hub to one-line rows and "Roles and addresses" is
the one hinted row,

claims.statement: The transport flow section has five pages, shown on the task list as three rows: arrival details, transit countries and transporter.
claims.quote:
The transport flow section has five pages. The hub does not render that
section directly. It renders three task rows: arrival details, transit
countries and transporter.

claims.statement: A task row's statuses are Not yet started, In progress, Completed, Optional and Not applicable.
claims.quote:
for Not yet started, In
  progress, Completed, Optional or Not applicable states

claims.statement: An incomplete mandatory task row holds back submission: the task list still offers the review, and it is the Check your answers submit that refuses.
claims.quote:
Every task row participates in `readyForCheckYourAnswers`. A mandatory new row
therefore holds the notification back from submission until it is complete —
the hub still offers the review, and the check-answers POST is what refuses.

claims.statement: On Check your answers, summary rows carry no Change link: each card's heading carries the one Change link for every answer inside it.
claims.quote:
Rows carry no Change link: the card's
heading carries the one link for every answer inside it,

claims.statement: On Check your answers, a stored code is shown through its service label, and a conditional row is shown only while its answer is in scope.
claims.quote:
Use a service label function when
the stored value is a code. Show a conditional row only while the same
obligation path is in scope.

claims.statement: A conditional field that is out of scope is not shown, validated or saved, and any stored value is removed when it leaves scope.
claims.quote:
For a conditional field, use `scope.has(fieldName)` to decide whether to render
and validate it. Do not commit a hidden value. The evaluator removes stored
data when the obligation leaves scope.

claims.statement: An invalid submission re-shows the user's raw entries with status 400; a recoverable save failure re-shows the same entries with a recoverable-error message and status 500.
claims.quote:
3. re-renders raw values with status 400 on error
4. commits cleaned values with `state.commit()`
5. redirects through `await kit.nextTarget(request, page, committed.scope)`

Wrap the write in `kit.recoverableSave()`. A marked persistence failure renders
the same values with `recoverableError: true` and status 500.

claims.statement: Each error-summary link targets the field by its id and moves focus to the control.
claims.quote:
Keep the input name, input id and validation error key the same. This lets the
error-summary link target `#<fieldName>` and move focus to the control.

claims.statement: A field the backend notification has no home for is kept out of the backend payload rather than given an invented property.
claims.quote:
If the backend has no field home, leave the mapper unchanged and add or update
an explicit omission assertion. Do not invent a payload property.

claims.statement: The backend payload has two projections: Mapper B layers its extra fields over Mapper A, so the saved answers can hold values one projection cannot represent.
claims.quote:
Canonical fulfilment can contain values that one backend projection cannot
represent. Mapper B layers its additional fields over Mapper A.

claims.statement: Positions in a collection (line0, unit1) are not durable record ids: every save replaces the whole snapshot, and removing an earlier item can renumber later ones.
claims.quote:
Grouped fulfilment tokens such as `line0` and `unit1` are positions in one canonical
snapshot, not durable record identifiers. Removing an earlier entry can renumber
later entries.

claims.statement: On the documents page, Add validates the entry, appends it and redirects back to the page for the next one.
claims.quote:
`action === 'add'` validates the entry
fields, appends, and redirects back to the page for the next one.

claims.statement: On the documents page, Continue also adds the entry when the trader has started one (chosen a document type), and otherwise moves on without saving anything.
claims.quote:
Continue
posts the same entry fields with it, so it appends too when the payload holds
a started entry — `startsADocument` in
[`form/payload.js`](../journeys/linear/features/documents/form/payload.js)
keys that on the trader having chosen a document type — and otherwise advances
with no write.

claims.statement: Every successful document add ends in a redirect, so reloading the page never adds the document twice, and an unsaved draft is never stored as a half-created entry.
claims.quote:
so every successful append ends in a redirect rather than
a render: the POST mutated state and a reload must not replay it. The append
creates the snapshot-local position — until that POST the draft lives only in
the payload, never a half-created instance in the store:

claims.statement: Removing a document is a form button (not a link a GET can trigger); an index the collection has no entry for is refused.
claims.quote:
Remove is a third branch of the same POST — a submit button named
`action` with a `remove:<index>` value, so the page form's crumb travels
with it and no GET can trigger a delete.

claims.statement: Saving the commodity search creates one commodity line per selected species, keeps a still-selected line's data (including its identifier records) and deletes a deselected line.
claims.quote:
`reconcileEntriesAt` keys existing instances by `keyOf`, keeps a still-selected
line's data (including its nested identifier records), and drops a deselected
line with wipe semantics.

claims.statement: The consignment details page shows a table of the selected commodities with a Remove per commodity and an Add another link, and edits every line's quantities in place.
claims.quote:
collects nothing (`collects: []`), renders the selected-commodities table with a
per-commodity Remove and an Add-another link, and edits every line's quantities
in place

claims.statement: Animal identifiers are collected with one card per commodity line on the identification page.
claims.quote:
The `animalIdentifiers` collection lives one level down, one card per commodity
line.

claims.statement: A collection reached from a Change link on Check your answers keeps that context through its add, remove and save round-trips; only its final Continue returns to Check your answers, and a return to the task list wins first.
claims.quote:
Only the exit repoints to check-your-answers;
mid-loop actions must never bounce there early.

claims.statement: A line's animal-identifier records are capped at that line's number of animals; adding one at the cap is refused, and an unanswered number of animals means no cap.
claims.quote:
Each `animalIdentifiers` collection is capped at its line's
`numberOfAnimalsQuantity`.

claims.statement: Removing an identifier record with an out-of-range or non-integer index is refused, so a malformed remove cannot create a phantom line or delete the first record.
claims.quote:
`isValidIndex` in
   [`src/server/app/engine/write/pipeline/predicates.js`](../../../engine/write/pipeline/predicates.js) uses `Number.isInteger` because
   `splice(NaN, 1)` coerces to `splice(0, 1)` — a malformed remove URL would
   otherwise destroy the first instance.

claims.statement: When one field of a collection entry leaves scope, only that field's value is wiped; the entry itself is kept.
claims.quote:
When an instance falls out of scope, the engine wipes that instance's stale
value — a field-level wipe inside one instance, not a whole-instance delete.

claims.statement: A collection entry with no saved field is not persisted; an entry is committed only after validation produces at least one value.
claims.quote:
A leaf-less entry has no canonical record from which to infer an instance and
is therefore not persisted. Collection forms should commit an entry only after
validation has produced at least one bound leaf.

claims.statement: A field inside a collection can depend on an answer in the same entry or an enclosing one, but not on an answer in an unrelated sibling entry.
claims.quote:
It
cannot read a value in a sibling frame at the same depth.

claims.statement: Every changed page is checked with axe on its first render and its validation-error state, failing on any serious or critical WCAG 2 A or AA violation.
claims.quote:
Every changed page needs happy-path and validation coverage. Axe checks cover the
initial page and its validation-error state, failing on serious or critical WCAG 2 A
or AA violations.

claims.statement: The transport group's accessibility checks also run the WCAG 2.1 and 2.2 rule tags (wcag21a, wcag21aa, wcag22aa).
claims.quote:
Its tags are
`wcag2a`, `wcag2aa`, `wcag21a`, `wcag21aa` and `wcag22aa`

claims.statement: Each browser feature test starts its own notification.
claims.quote: Each feature test starts its own notification.

claims.statement: Lighthouse audits 19 fixed URLs once each with the desktop preset, signing in through the Defra ID stub first.
claims.quote:
- collects 19 literal URLs on `http://localhost:3000`
- runs each URL once
- uses the desktop preset

claims.statement: Lighthouse fails a page below 0.60 for performance, 0.70 for accessibility or 0.70 for best practices; there is no SEO assertion.
claims.quote:
| Performance    | 0.60    |
| Accessibility  | 0.70    |
| Best practices | 0.70    |

There is no SEO assertion.

claims.statement: Lighthouse scores are not lowered without agreement, and removing an audited URL needs a recorded reason.
claims.quote:
Do not lower a score to make a change pass without agreement. Record why a URL
is removed.

claims.statement: Lighthouse runs in CI after a branch image is published (or by hand), keeps its report for 14 days and publishes it to GitHub Pages.
claims.quote:
`.github/workflows/lighthouse.yml` runs after a successful branch image
publish, or by manual dispatch.

claims.statement: Existing ruling: pages are the journey spine; a page has an id, a slug and the answers it collects, and that one identity drives dispatch, gates and navigation.
claims.quote:
## Pages are the journey spine

A page descriptor has an `id`, a `slug` and page-owned `collects`. The same identity
is used by dispatch, gates and navigation.

claims.statement: Existing ruling: shared code is a library that never discovers features or imports a set; set and journey policy is supplied through explicit configuration.
claims.quote:
## Shared code is a library

Controllers call small functions from `shared/`, `lib/`, `engine/` and `flow/`.
Those modules do not discover features or import a set.

claims.statement: Existing ruling: the model decides what is in scope and whether it is mandatory or optional; the journey decides page order; task rows decide grouping on the task list.
claims.quote:
## The model owns applicability; the journey owns sequence

The obligation evaluator decides what is in scope and whether it is mandatory or
optional. Journey sections decide page order. Task rows decide how work is grouped
on a hub.

claims.statement: Existing ruling: page and section gates are derived by default from page ownership, scope and prerequisites; an authored gate is reserved for policy the derived rule cannot express.
claims.quote:
## Gates are derived by default

[`src/server/app/flow/gates.js`](../flow/gates.js) derives normal page and section
gates from dispatch ownership, scope and prerequisites. Authored gates are reserved
for journey policy that the derived rule cannot represent.

claims.statement: Existing ruling: each answer is owned by exactly one page; duplicate or missing ownership is rejected, and a page claims a collection's root rather than each nested field.
claims.quote:
## One obligation has one page owner

[`src/server/app/flow/dispatch.js`](../flow/dispatch.js) rejects duplicate and
missing ownership.

claims.statement: Existing ruling: the model holds no display copy; labels, hints, options, validation messages and templates belong to the journey, and a boot-time purity check rejects display-shaped keys in the model.
claims.quote:
## The model has no display copy

Obligations contain stable domain identity, scope, mandate and invariants. Journeys
own labels, hints, options, validation messages and templates. Boot-time purity
checks reject display-shaped keys in the model.

claims.statement: Existing ruling: the bridge is the only seam between the model and the pages; a journey registers its field bindings with it.
claims.quote: ## The bridge is the model-to-page seam

claims.statement: Existing ruling: composition is explicit; only a set's own gateway knows which set and journey exist, and the model, bridge, engine and flow receive their policy keyed by set id.
claims.quote:
## Composition is explicit

A set's own gateway — today
[`routes-live-animals.js`](../routes-live-animals.js),

claims.statement: Platform limit: the obligation model is executable code (scope rules are functions), not portable JSON configuration.
claims.quote:
Obligation `applyTo` rules are JavaScript functions. Helper metadata makes their
dependencies inspectable, but the manifest is not portable JSON configuration.

claims.statement: Platform limit: a page's derived gate opens when at least one answer it collects is in scope and its prerequisites pass.
claims.quote:
The normal page gate passes when at least one collected obligation is in scope and
its prerequisites pass.

claims.statement: Platform limit: a list-valued answer (such as species) cannot drive a single-value scope gate; collection conditions use group-aware rules instead.
claims.quote:
The standard scalar gate helpers expect scalar fulfilment values. Collection
conditions use group-aware helpers and cardinality rules instead.

claims.statement: Platform limit: ownership of nested collection fields is derived from the collection root a page claims; no second page may own a nested field.
claims.quote: Do not declare a second page owner for a nested leaf.

claims.statement: Platform limit: saving is not transactional across backend projections; a partial failure is reported to the user as a recoverable backend error.
claims.quote:
Real persistence can update
more than one backend projection, and adapter code is responsible for reporting
partial failures as recoverable backend errors.

claims.statement: Field and collection names must not contain a dot or square brackets; the service refuses to start otherwise.
claims.quote:
They must be path-safe — no `.`, `[` or `]` — or `buildDispatch` throws at
  boot

claims.statement: The notification field poApprovedReferenceNumber is bound under a 'system' feature with no page, so it is filled in by the system rather than answered by the user.
claims.note: Inferred from the 'system' feature having no page. The obligation outside this slice (obligations/sections/system.js) confirms it is system-assigned at notification creation in the form GBN-AG-YY-XXXXXX.

claims.statement: Mounting the live-animals set also runs boot-time checks on obligation purity, that every obligation has a fulfilment binding, and that address party bindings are scalar, so a gap in any of these stops the service starting.
claims.quote:
assertObligationPurity()
        assertFulfilmentBindingCoverage()
        assertPartyBindingsAreScalar()
claims.note: Inferred from the assert-named calls inside plugin registration; what each checks lives outside this slice.

claims.statement: A date field left blank is read as an empty day, month and year, rather than as an unreadable date.

claims.statement: The commodity reference service (commodity and species options, the Cow Domestic/Game type mapping and the obligation allow-lists) belongs to the live-animals set; its vocabulary is not a generic platform contract.
claims.quote:
The commodities reference service belongs to the live-animals set:
...
It provides commodity and species options, the Cow Domestic/Game type mapping and
the allow-lists used by live-animals obligations and pages. This vocabulary is not a
generic platform contract.

claims.statement: The commodities task row claims its share of the commodity line by exclusion, so a new field added to the commodity line counts towards the commodities row by default rather than falling out of all three rows.
claims.quote:
The `commodities` row claims its
facet with `except` rather than `only`, so a new member of the collection defaults
to that row instead of falling out of all three.

claims.statement: A blank number of animals removes the identifier cap but cannot let the notification finish early: the per-line floor on identifier records still applies at submit.
claims.quote:
An **unanswered
count is deliberately no cap** — the per-instance floor still bites at submit,
so a blank count never lets a journey finish early.

claims.statement: A collection counts as complete only when its minimum-entries floor is met and every entry in it is complete.
claims.quote:
answers whether one instance is complete; the group is complete when its
  `requires` floor is met and every instance is complete.

claims.statement: Removing a document reconciles the notification, so any answer left out of scope by the removal is pruned in the same write.
claims.quote:
It splices the instance out and
reconciles, so anything left dangling out of scope is pruned too

claims.statement: Lighthouse signs in at the Defra ID stub as user 2100010101, using AUTH_PASSWORD or the stub password when that is not set.
claims.quote:
If it finds the Defra ID stub form, it
signs in with user `2100010101`. It reads the password from `AUTH_PASSWORD` and
uses the stub password when that variable is absent.

claims.statement: Lighthouse audits literal paths only, so journey pages, whose routes carry a notification id, are not audited until there is a reliable way to create or seed that id.
claims.quote:
The list contains literal paths. Journey routes include a notification ID, so
they need a reliable way to create or seed that ID before they can replace a
literal audit URL.

claims.statement: The Lighthouse CI run builds a score index page and a flagged-audits file of weighted audits scoring below 1 in the three asserted categories (SEO excluded), and passes the result, report URL and flagged findings to the workspace status action.
claims.quote:
It records weighted numeric or binary audits with
a score below 1 for the three asserted categories.

claims.statement: The commodity details (entry) sub-page sits in a section of its own, so Continue on the commodities list page leaves the commodity section rather than running on into the details page; the details page is reached from the list and returns to it.
claims.quote:
The commodity entry sub-page sits in a section of its own rather than after
 * the list page it belongs to. `nextInSection` sends a page's Continue to the

 * commodity section altogether — the entry page is reached from the list and

claims.statement: The commodity details sub-page's own section still gives it the commodity-type prerequisite that every page after the entry question carries.
claims.quote:
Its own section still gives it
 * the commodity-type prerequisite that every page after the entry question
 * carries.

claims.statement: Origin comes after the commodity details sub-page, because the origin answer is enforced at Continue for every page after it, and placing it earlier would stop a trader adding a commodity line until they had named a country.
claims.quote:
Origin follows the entry sub-page rather than preceding it. Its answer is
 * enforced at Continue, so every page placed after it needs one; ahead of the

 * named a country.

claims.statement: The arrival section opens on the arrival status question, whose answer decides what the rest of the section asks for, and goes on to the arrival details page.
claims.quote:
The arrival section opens on the arrival-status question, whose answer
 * decides what the rest of the section asks for, and goes on to the arrival

claims.statement: Potato notifications never see the arrival status question: it is out of scope for them, so both the opening run and the hub's arrival row skip it and land on arrival details, which every commodity type answers.

Potato notifications never see the question: `arrivalStatus` is out
 * of scope for them, so the derived page gate fails and both the opening run

 * landing on arrival-details instead — a page every commodity type answers.

claims.statement: The place of destination is a section of its own after the arrival section, so Continue on arrival details leaves the arrival section rather than running on into the destination page.

The opening run asks the arrival status ahead of it — that order is `RUN_STEPS`
 * in run.js, not this array — so the page usually has a status to work from and
 * shows the right one of its three questions. It is not a prerequisite: a
 * trader entering from the hub with no status answered gets the pre-arrival
 * question, which is what the page falls back to.

claims.statement: The parties section holds the consignor page then the identification numbers page.

claims.statement: The contact section holds only the consignment contact address page.

claims.statement: The full UI journey answers every section in this order: origin (France, region code Yes 75, internal reference Imports456GB), commodity (Bos taurus, 1 animal, 5 packages), identification (ear tag UK123456789012), reason (Internal market, Breeding) and additional details (Slaughter, unweaned No), addresses and CPH (12/345/6789), transport (road vehicle, transited France and Belgium, García Livestock Transport SL), then contact (Animal and Plant Health Agency).

The default test notification shared by the UI journey and the seeder is: country France, commodity Dog, type Domestic, species Bison bison and Bos spp., reason internal market, animals 5 and 19, packages 13 and 21, certification approvedBodies, port Aberdeen Airport, arrival 14 days ahead and means of transport Vessel.
claims.quote:
countryCode: countryCodes.eu.france,
...
  commodityCode: commodityCodes.dog,
  commodityType: commodityTypes.domestic,
  species: [commoditySpecies.bisonBison, commoditySpecies.bosSpp],
  importReason: importReasons.internalMarket,
  noOfAnimals: [5, 19],
  noOfPackages: [13, 21],
  certificationPurpose: certificationPurposes.approvedBodies,
...
  pointOfEntry: pointOfEntries.aberdeen,
  arrivalDate: getRelativeDateInput({ dayOffset: 14 }),
  meansOfTransport: meansOfTransport.vessel,
claims.note: The default pairs a Dog commodity code with cattle species (Bison bison, Bos spp.); the UI journey helper does not use these defaults (it searches Bos taurus).

claims.statement: Add the county parish holding number (CPH) (caption Consignment parties) asks for the CPH number in three parts, County, Parish and Holding number, with an explanation in a details component.
claims.quote: CPH number — For example, 12/345/6789. ; County ; Parish ; Holding number ; A county parish holding (CPH) number is a unique 9-digit number used to identify land and buildings where livestock are kept, moved or handled. You can find your CPH number on documents from the Animal and Plant Health Agency (APHA).
claims.note: The three fields reuse govuk-date-input layout classes for a non-date input.

claims.statement: Arrival details (caption Transport and arrival) asks Arrival date at port of entry (MOJ date picker), Port of entry (autocomplete), Means of transport to the port of entry, Transport identification and Transport document reference.

Start typing to search by port or airport name or code. ; Means of transport to the port of entry ; Transport identification ; Transport document reference — Enter the reference number on the air waybill, bill of lading, sea waybill, road consignment note (CMR) or other transport document.
